div.l: Incipit liber Galfrid Chaucer de gestis peregrinoꝝorum versus Cantuariam
WHan that Aprille with his showres soote
The drowhte of marche hath ꝑperced to the roote
And bathed eủery veyne in such licour
Of which v̉ertu gendred is the flour
Whan Zepherus eek wᵗith his swete breth
Inspired hath eủery holt ⁊and heth
The tendre croppis and the yonge sonne
Hath in the Ram half cours I ronne
And smale fowles maketh melodie
That slepyn al the nyght with opyn eye
So prikketh hem nature in here corages
That longen folk to gon in pilgrimages
And palmeris for to seken straıı̄unge strondes
To fern halwes couthe in many londys
And specially fro euery sherys ende
Of engelond to to Cantirbury they wende
The holy blysfull martir for to sieke
That hem hath holpen whan they were sieke
Be fel that in that seson on a day
In southwerk at the tabbard as I lay
Redy to wende in my pilgrimage
To Cantirbury with ful devout corage
That nyht vere come in to that hostelery
Wel nyne ⁊and twenty in on company
Of sondry folk by aventure Falle
In felawshepe and pilgrymes were they alle
That toward Cantibury wolde they ride
The Chambres and the stables were wyde
And wel we weren esed at the beste
And schortly whan the sonne was gon to Reste
So hadde I spoken with hem everichon
That I was of here felashepe a noon
And maad forward erly for taryse
To take owr͗ way ther as I yow devyse
